description:
Redwood Inference has identified suspected runtime GPU memory fragmentation under sustained inference load (hours-long, mixed prompt lengths and concurrency) leading to gradual VRAM growth, allocator churn, and eventual OOMs or forced request shedding. The goal of this project is to (1) reproduce and precisely profile the fragmentation behavior across key GPU SKUs and model families, (2) determine the dominant fragmentation sources (e.g., KV cache block sizing/eviction patterns, temporary activation buffers, kernel workspace allocations, allocator bucket behavior, CUDA graph capture interactions), and (3) ship a mitigation patch that stabilizes steady-state VRAM usage without materially regressing throughput/latency.

Scope:
- In-scope: runtime memory allocation paths on GPU (KV cache, workspace buffers, temporary tensors), scheduler/batching behavior that drives allocation patterns, allocator configuration changes, new telemetry/metrics for fragmentation, reproducible soak tests, safe rollout and release notes.
- Out-of-scope: major architectural rewrites (new allocator from scratch), model accuracy changes, or customer-facing API changes (unless required for debug toggles/telemetry).

Key stakeholders and roles:
- Executive/engineering sponsor: Mateo Alvarez (VP Engineering, Runtime)
- Runtime execution/architecture: Noah Patel (Sr Staff), Omar El-Sayed, Samir Qureshi
- Kernel team: Hiro Tanaka (EM), Grace Kim, Yuki Sato
- Scheduling team: Sofia Ivanova (EM), Lena Fischer, Marcus Reed
- SRE/incident coordination: Neha Kapoor (VP Infra & Reliability), Sean Gallagher (Dir SRE), Rafael Mendes (SRE Mgr)
- Observability/telemetry: Allison Grant, Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman, Caleb Johnson
- Release train: Connor O’Brien (Release Eng Lead), Sahana Iyer

Phases / timeline (hypothetical):
1) Detection + reproduction (Week 1): correlate OOM events with traffic patterns; build a soak test recipe in perf-canary/benchmark-lab; confirm on at least 2 GPU SKUs.
2) Instrumentation + profiling (Weeks 1–2): add allocator/KV cache metrics, periodic memory snapshots, and GPU memory map summaries; run controlled experiments varying block sizes, batch composition, and cache eviction.
3) Mitigation design (Week 2): choose mitigation(s) such as KV cache block size normalization, periodic compaction/defragmentation, pooling of common workspace sizes, allocator arena resets at safe boundaries, and scheduler changes to reduce pathological churn.
4) Implementation + validation (Weeks 2–3): land runtime patch behind a kill-switch flag; run perf/regression suite; validate steady-state VRAM and tail latency.
5) Rollout + comms (Week 3–4): staged canary in one region, expand to all hosted pools; prepare enterprise/LTS guidance; update runbooks and known-issues docs.

Deliverables:
- Linear project with tracked work items and acceptance criteria
- Reproducible soak test and benchmark artifacts
- New metrics/dashboards + alerting guidance for fragmentation/OOM early warning
- Runtime mitigation patch (feature-flagged, with rollback)
- Release notes + operational runbook updates
- (If applicable) customer support ticket resolution and incident follow-up/retro

files.description: Linear project umbrella ticket: “GPU memory fragmentation investigation + mitigation”. Problem statement, goals/non-goals, success metrics (steady-state VRAM delta/hr), links to dashboards, and sub-issues.
Reproduction task: define sustained-load scenario (mixed prompt lengths, concurrency, streaming) and confirm VRAM growth on A100 + H100 pools; includes commands/configs and expected traces.
Instrumentation task: add allocator/KV cache fragmentation metrics (free/used blocks, largest-free-chunk, allocation rate, eviction rate) and periodic snapshots gated by config.
Profiling task: run controlled matrix varying KV block size, batch policy, CUDA graphs on/off; record VRAM slope and fragmentation indicators; includes analysis notes and open questions.
Mitigation design task: evaluate options (pooling, block-size normalization, compaction, allocator tuning). Captures trade-offs and proposed guarded rollout plan.
Implementation task: runtime patch (feature-flagged) to reduce fragmentation (e.g., KV cache allocation strategy + workspace pooling). Acceptance criteria and testing checklist.
Perf/regression validation task: extend perf suite to include 6–12 hour soak; thresholds for VRAM slope, p95/p99 latency, throughput, and error rates.
Rollout task: canary in one hosted region + dedicated pool; monitoring plan, rollback conditions, comms template for on-call.
Docs/runbook task: update profiling playbook + known-issues + release notes with fragmentation guidance and operational steps.

Confluence playbook page: step-by-step guide to run fragmentation soak tests, collect allocator stats, GPU memory snapshots, and interpret fragmentation metrics; includes “when to page runtime” guidance.
ADR describing the chosen mitigation approach (e.g., KV cache block normalization + workspace pooling), alternatives considered, risks, operational toggles, and rollback strategy.
Known-issues entry: symptoms, affected versions/models/SKUs, detection signals, temporary mitigations (restart cadence, config changes), and link to fixed release.
Dashboard spec for new fragmentation panels: VRAM slope, allocator churn, largest-free-block %, KV cache occupancy/evictions, and recommended alerts.
SRE runbook updates: triage steps for increasing OOMs, safe restarts vs pool drains, config toggles to reduce churn, escalation criteria, and links to incident workflows.
Runtime release notes entry for the mitigation patch: what changed, expected impact, compatibility notes, feature flag defaults, and operational monitoring tips.
PR: Add allocator/KV cache fragmentation metrics + periodic snapshot logging behind a runtime config flag; includes tests and example output.
PR: Implement mitigation in KV cache allocation (e.g., block-size normalization and/or improved free-list reuse) to reduce fragmentation under mixed decode workloads.
PR: Workspace buffer pooling for common kernel workspace sizes; reduces allocation churn across attention kernels; includes benchmark comparisons.
PR: Scheduler tweak to reduce pathological allocation patterns (e.g., avoid rapid oscillation between very short and very long sequences in the same batch window).
PR: Add long-running soak scenario (6–12h) with mixed prompt-length distribution; emits VRAM slope + fragmentation metrics to CI artifacts.
PR: Experiment harness for KV block size / compaction toggles; generates summary tables and plots (as text) for fragmentation comparison across SKUs.
PR: Add new dashboard panels/alerts for early-warning of fragmentation-driven OOMs; ties to runtime metrics introduced in redwood PRs.
PR: Hotfix release branch cherry-pick + default flag settings for hosted pools; includes rollback notes and release checklist from Release Engineering.
Working doc: experiment matrix (GPU SKU, model, batch policy, KV settings), raw observations, links to logs/dashboards, and hypotheses updated over time.
Working doc: pasted allocator snapshot excerpts, annotations of suspicious patterns (bucket saturation, large-free-block shrink), and questions for kernel/scheduling teams.
Spreadsheet-style table: per-run VRAM slope, allocation rate, eviction rate, largest-free-block %, p95 latency, throughput; includes a short interpretation section.
SRE analysis doc: timeline of OOM events, regions/pools impacted, correlation with deploys/traffic, and a proposed alert threshold for early detection.
Launch brief draft: rollout stages, canary pools, success metrics, rollback steps, and owner checklist for runtime-1.18.2.
Slack thread in #eng-runtime: initial report of VRAM creeping up during overnight load test; coordination to reproduce and gather first logs.
Slack thread in #eng-runtime: discussion of likely fragmentation sources (KV cache vs workspace), proposed quick instrumentation points, and who will code what.
Slack thread in #eng-runtime: sharing allocator snapshot output and interpreting “largest free chunk” trend; request for kernel team input.
Slack thread in #eng-runtime: debate on mitigation approach (compaction vs pooling) and operational risk; decision to gate behind kill-switch.
Slack thread in #eng-runtime: perf results from soak runs; notes on p99 latency deltas and VRAM stabilization after patch.
Slack thread in #eng-platform: telemetry team coordinating new metric ingestion/cardinality concerns for allocator/KV metrics and dashboard needs.
Slack thread in #eng-sre: SRE flags rising OOM rate in one hosted pool; asks runtime for mitigation timeline and immediate operational steps.
Slack incident thread in #incidents: incident bot timeline, impact assessment, mitigations (pool drain/restart), and handoff to runtime investigation.
Slack thread in #eng-releases: release engineering coordinating cherry-picks, CI soak gates, and go/no-go criteria for hotfix rollout.
Slack thread in #postmortems: collecting contributing factors and action items for follow-up doc (alerts, soak tests, runbook gaps).
Customer support ticket: enterprise customer reports periodic OOMs after ~8 hours sustained traffic on Dedicated; includes logs, model/version, and workaround requests; links to incident and PRs.
Internal support/helpdesk ticket: request to add/adjust on-call alerting for VRAM slope / allocator churn and document the new dashboard for SRE.
Email thread (leadership/manager coordination): Neha Kapoor, Mateo Alvarez, Sean Gallagher, Connor O’Brien align on customer impact, hotfix timeline, rollout risk, and comms plan.

Fireflies transcript: technical deep dive with an enterprise customer (Dedicated) about observed OOMs under sustained load; Redwood runtime + SRE explain investigation, proposed mitigation, and interim operational guidance.
